summary_html: A **state agency fails** to meet federal child-welfare performance standards, triggering **funding penalties** or corrective action under the CFSR or Single Audit Act.
authority_html:
- **Child & Family Services Reviews (45 CFR Part 1355)** — performance oversight and penalties  
- **Single Audit Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 7501–7507)** — audit of federally funded programs  
- **Inspector General Act (5 U.S.C. App.)** — oversight authority for HHS/OIG

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court reversed the court of appeals and held that the county's reasonable efforts to reunite were supported by clear and convincing evidence, explaining that reasonable efforts are assessed after statutory grounds and best interests are established.
key_cases.relevance: Reasonable efforts is the Title IV-E condition on federal reimbursement, and this case sets Minnesota's judicial test for it.
key_cases.quote: the appellate court then determines whether there is clear and convincing evidence that the county made reasonable efforts to reunite the family

key_cases.holding: The court held that when parental rights are terminated for palpable unfitness the district court must still determine whether reasonable efforts to rehabilitate and reunify were made, even if the determination is that services would be unrealistic.
key_cases.relevance: It embeds the federal Title IV-E reasonable-efforts condition into a mandatory Minnesota judicial finding.
key_cases.quote: provision of reasonable efforts must be evaluated by the court in every case

key_cases.case_name: In re Welfare of the Child of E.A.C.
key_cases.holding: The court held that on a challenge to an ICWA petition for return of custody the agency bears the burden of proving active efforts and the serious-damage finding beyond a reasonable doubt, and remanded for application of that standard.
key_cases.relevance: It is the strictest Minnesota statement of the agency's evidentiary burden on the efforts requirement that federal funding is conditioned upon.
key_cases.quote: the burden of proof to determine whether active efforts have been made is beyond a reasonable doubt and rests with the agency responsible for providing the remedial services

state_agency.name: Minnesota Department of Children, Youth, and Families
state_agency.hotline: No statewide hotline. Call the county or Tribal child protection agency where the child lives — the directory link is on dcyf.mn.gov/individuals-and-families/report-abuse

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Filing of the appealable juvenile court order
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified by statute; Minn. Stat. § 260C.415, subd. 1 requires the appeal to be taken within 30 days of the filing of the appealable order.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: Receipt of notice of the investigating agency's final determination regarding maltreatment
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in Minn. Stat. § 260E.33; subd. 2 requires the written request within 15 calendar days after receipt of notice of the final determination, subd. 3 allows a fair hearing only after the agency denies the reconsideration request or fails to act on it within 15 working days, and subd. 1 provides no reconsideration after a family assessment or noncaregiver human trafficking assessment because no maltreatment determination is made.
